newsitem.title: MOZAMBIQUE: Soccer-Namibia dent Mozambique's chances in Castle Cup.
newsitem.headline: Soccer-Namibia dent Mozambique's chances in Castle Cup.

text.p: Mozambique lost an opportunity to go clear ahead in the Cosafa Castle Cup standings after being held 1-1 by Namibia in their final round group competition match on Sunday.
Early dominance and a 19th minute goal by Pinto Barros promised a comfortable win for the home team in the new southern African regional tournament but Namibia came back strongly to share the spoils.
Mozambique squandered several good first-half opportunities -- including a shot from midfielder Jossias that struck a post -- before Silvester Goraseb got an equaliser for Namibia on half-time.
Goraseb headed home a cross from German-based winger Eliphas Shivute, who created more chances after the break for the visitors.
Striker Gervatius Uri Khob missed from close range and Shivute himself shot wide as Mozambique surprisingly crumbled in the second-half.
The result does see Mozambique go top the table but only by virtue of having scored more goals than Namibia, who also have five points and the same goal difference.
But Sunday's match was Mozambique's final home match in the tournament, who carries almost $200,000 in prize money, and leaves them with an uphill task in their final game away to Zambia on August 2.
Namibia still have a home match to come against Zambia at the end of August. Zambia are lurking in third place with four points and two games to come.
Each teams plays the other side once only in the final round group competition, which also features Malawi and Tanzania.

Namibia: 1-Fillemon Kanalelo; 2-Petrus Haraseb, 5-Bimbo Tjihero, 14-Stanley Gogoaseb, 17-Robert Nauseb; 12-Mohammed Ouseb, 4-Frans Ananias, 18-Paul Bostander, 6-Silvester Goraseb; 3-Eliphas Shivute (7-Razandura Tjikuzu 88th minute), 8-Gervatius Uri Kob.
